nodes.label: User typing
nodes.summary: Types into a search box and expects suggestions to keep up with each keystroke.

nodes.label: Browser client
nodes.summary: Preloads the user's own connections on focus and caches results so similar queries skip the backend (Facebook). Debounce and request cancellation are our additions.

nodes.label: Edge cache
nodes.summary: Caches responses for popular short prefixes that are not personalised. Our reference design.

nodes.label: Typeahead aggregator
nodes.summary: Stateless, with no index of its own: fans the query out to leaf services in parallel, merges and ranks their results, and returns ids (Facebook's aggregator).

nodes.label: Global prefix index
nodes.summary: Unpersonalised index of pages, applications or popular queries; results are the same for everyone, so recent results are kept in a memcached query cache (Facebook). Query completion serves per-prefix top-k from an in-memory structure.

nodes.label: Network typeahead
nodes.summary: Personalised index over the user's graph neighbourhood. Cleo keeps an in-memory adjacency list, a per-document Bloom filter and a forward index per partition, and serves in about 20 ms on average.

nodes.label: Web tier
nodes.summary: Fetches names and pictures for the returned ids from memcache and MySQL, and checks the searcher may see each result.

nodes.label: Query logs
nodes.summary: Past searches; Google says its predictions reflect searches that have been done, adjusted for language, location and freshness.

nodes.label: Index builder
nodes.summary: Batch job: normalise and count queries, apply the policy filter, build per-prefix top-k lists, ship a versioned index. A streaming job adds a trending overlay. Our reference design.

nodes.label: Policy filter
nodes.summary: Blocks violent, sexually explicit, hateful, disparaging or dangerous predictions and those unlikely to lead to reliable content; enforcement teams remove what gets through (Google). The serving-time deny list is our addition.

steps.caption: The user types; the browser first answers from results it preloaded on focus and from its cache.
If the cache has too few results, it sends the prefix (and what it already shows).
Popular unpersonalised prefixes are answered at the edge; the rest reach the aggregator.
The global index returns prefix matches, often from its query cache.
In parallel, the network index returns matches from the user's connections.
The aggregator merges and ranks; the web tier fetches display data, checks privacy and returns the list.
The builder counts normalised queries over a decayed window and drops rare ones.
Candidates pass the policy filter; harmful or unreliable predictions are removed.
A new immutable index version is shipped and swapped in atomically on each server.
The network index misses its deadline, for example during a partition rebalance.
The aggregator returns what the global index sent rather than wait; a late answer is a wrong answer for typeahead.
The automated filter missed a policy-violating prediction and it is reported.
It is blocked at once by a serving-time deny list, then removed with its close variants in the next build.
